summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, diabetes, and a history of failed kidney transplant was admitted for fevers and rigors that occurred during a dialysis session. He reported subjective low-grade fevers for about a week. Initial evaluation included a chest X-ray and ultrasound of the dialysis fistula, both of which showed no acute abnormalities. Blood cultures were negative for growth. He was treated with IV vancomycin and gentamicin initially, but antibiotics were discontinued as he improved clinically and remained afebrile. A vascular study revealed mild-to-moderate tibial occlusive disease, likely contributing to chronic foot ulcers. The patient stabilized, and after reassessment, was discharged home with instructions to continue follow-up with podiatry and manage his chronic conditions. No surgical procedures were performed during this admission.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
